title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 435
paragraphs: It is clear to me, therefore, by every kind of proof, that Cambyses was exceedingly mad; for otherwise he would not have undertaken to mock religious rites and customary observances. For if one were to propose to all men a choice, bidding them select the best customs out of all the customs that exist, each race, after examining them all, would choose those of their own people; thus all think their own customs by far the best. And so it is unlikely that anyone but a madman would make jest of such things. That all men are accustomed to think this way about their customs, we may judge by many other proofs and especially by the following. Darius, in the course of his reign, summoned those of the Greeks who were present in his land and asked them for what price they would consent to eat the bodies of their fathers when they died; and they answered that for no price would they do so. After this Darius summoned those Indians who are called Callatians, who eat their parents, and asked them in the presence of the Greeks — who understood what was said by help of an interpreter — for what payment they would consent to burn the bodies of their fathers when they died; and they cried out loud and begged him to keep silence from such words. Thus, then, these things are established by custom, and I think Pindar spoke rightly in his verse when he said that “of all things, law is king.”
